required_tuples.rationale: Public GET /status on the initialized fixture answers 200 with app audiobookshelf, serverVersion 2.37.2, isInit true, language en-us, authMethods [local], authFormData present and no ConfigPath/MetadataPath, identically on repetition.
An invalid bearer token does not change the public /status body and POST /status answers 404 because only router.get is registered.
A cold uninitialised install answers isInit false with the actual ConfigPath and MetadataPath directories and an empty user table.
GET /ping answers 200 with success true without credentials on every call.
POST /ping is not registered and answers 404 while GET keeps succeeding.
With ROUTER_BASE_PATH=/audiobookshelf the bare /ping is rewritten to the prefixed route and answers the same body.
GET /healthcheck answers 200 with the plain body OK without credentials on every call.
POST /healthcheck answers 404 because only the GET route exists.
HEAD /healthcheck answers 200 with an empty body and a query parameter does not change the OK answer.
/, /library/:id, /library/:id/search, /item/:id, /author/:id, /config/users/:id, /collection/:id and /playlist/:id answer 200 text/html with the same unauthenticated entry document.
/favicon.ico is served with a non-empty non-entry body while a missing asset and a directory path answer 404 without the SPA fallback or a listing.
Query strings and the optional bookshelf/series segments serve the entry document while an unlisted client-shaped path answers 404.
Authenticated unmatched /api paths answer 404 and are never rewritten into the client entry document.
The /api auth gate answers 401 before route matching, so an unmatched path is not a 404 for an unauthenticated caller.
Registered routes keep their own status: /api/me 200, unknown method on /api/libraries 404, /ping public, /api/backups 401 unauthenticated; the terminal handler only exists with REACT_CLIENT_PATH.
GET /api/libraries returns the two fixture libraries with their folders, repeats the body and ETag, answers 304 to a matching If-None-Match with an empty body and still answers a random sort.
GET /api/libraries answers 401 without a token and with an invalid token and changes no library row.
Library GETs are scoped to the caller's accessible libraries and a committed rename is visible to the root and restricted caller on the next GET.

The unauthenticated item cover answers the Capacitor and localhost origins with the exact grant (echoed origin, all methods, headers *, credentials true) while serving the image, and the ebook route does the same with a token.
An unlisted origin on the mobile cover path and the mobile origin on the non-mobile /api/libraries path receive no grant, while the cover is still served and the API still answers 401.
OPTIONS on the mobile cover path answers 200 OK with the grant for both mobile origins, and 401 without a grant for an unlisted origin or without an Origin header.
Status, ping, an authenticated API route and a static asset answer the same status and body under /audiobookshelf and under their bare path through the legacy rewrite.
Three consecutive cover requests from the Capacitor origin return the same image bytes and the same complete grant.
After the admin adds an allowed origin, that origin receives the grant on /api/libraries while an unrelated origin receives none.
With ALLOW_CORS=1 an arbitrary origin receives the grant on an ordinary API path and an ebook preflight answers 200 with the grant.
The unauthenticated cover read answers 200, the ebook route answers 401 without and with an invalid token and returns no file bytes, and unknown item/author image ids answer 404 rather than 401.
A cold boot of an uninitialised install answers ping, uninitialised status, the client root and a 401 API with an empty user table, and creates metadata/streams and the config database.
A SIGINT shutdown is graceful (the harness fails on SIGKILL) and a restart on the same install serves the committed library rename and status again.
After SIGINT /ping no longer succeeds, the sqlite database file remains and the next boot serves ping again.
A socket connected after a restart authenticates, subscribes and receives the log event for a following ping while the HTTP API still serves.
Two restarts, a shutdown and another restart keep serving ping and the committed library name, including with scannerDisableWatcher toggled.
Boot removes a UUID-v4-named directory under metadata/streams, keeps a non-UUID directory and keeps the committed library rename.
A boot with CONFIG_PATH naming a regular file exits non-zero, /ping does not succeed, the file is unchanged and the install config directory stays empty.
One ping after an INFO subscription delivers exactly one log event with non-empty string timestamp/source/message, levelName INFO and level 2.
An ordinary-user socket and an unauthenticated socket that send set_log_listener receive no log event for later log lines.
A WARN subscription filters an INFO line while an INFO subscription receives it, and both subscriptions receive a later WARN line.
An authenticated socket that never sent set_log_listener receives no log event for two pings.
Three set_log_listener calls replace the entry: two pings deliver exactly two log events, not six.
Raising INFO to WARN stops INFO delivery, lowering it restores it, and remove_log_listener stops delivery entirely.
Levels 7, "2" and 0.5 are rejected by the integer/known-level check and the admin socket receives no log event.
The fixture install lists no backups, reports metadata/backups as the location, backupPathEnvSet false and an empty backup directory.

The created entry has a YYYY-MM-DDTHHmm id, key sqlite, version 2.37.2, id-based filename under backups/, the install backup directory, a current createdAt and fileSize equal to the only file on disk.
Applying a backup taken before a rename answers 200, reads back the pre-rename library name, keeps the backup listed and keeps the caller's token valid.
Ordinary users get 403 on list/create/upload, anonymous list gets 401, unknown apply/delete ids get 404, and the backup list and library row are unchanged.
Applying the same backup twice answers 200 both times and leaves the restored library name and backup count unchanged.
Applying the backup removes a user created after it, reverts a later library rename and keeps the pre-existing root token authenticating.
An archive without absdatabase.sqlite answers 500, a non-zip 400 and a wrong extension 500, with no backup entry, no leftover file, no library change and no backup_applied.
A successful apply delivers exactly one backup_applied to an admin and an ordinary authenticated socket and none to an unauthenticated socket.
A forbidden apply, an unknown id and a rejected upload deliver no backup_applied to admin or ordinary sockets.
The single apply event carries exactly one argument that serializes as null and decodes as nil, pinning the omitted data argument.
A socket connected after earlier applies receives exactly one event for the next apply it observes.
Two successful applies deliver exactly two events to the same socket.
A socket connected after an apply receives no replay of it and receives exactly one event for the next apply.
An archive that cannot be applied is rejected with 500, emits no backup_applied and leaves the backup list and library row unchanged.
Two admin sockets and one ordinary socket each receive one backup_applied while an unauthenticated socket receives none.
A forbidden apply by an ordinary user emits no backup_applied to admin, ordinary or anonymous sockets.
The broadcast event has exactly one JSON null argument for both an admin and a non-admin recipient.
A fresh admin socket holds no earlier event and receives the next apply's single event.
Two applies in a row deliver one event per apply to the same socket.
A late socket sees no past apply and then exactly one event for the next apply.
A rejected archive and an unknown backup id emit no backup_applied to admin, ordinary or anonymous sockets.

not_applicable.reason: confirmed: stateless public status read; the record's exception marks state scenarios not applicable and there is no persisted state to vary.
confirmed: stateless ping route; no persisted state.
confirmed: stateless healthcheck route; no persisted state.
confirmed: static client serving on a read-only dist directory; the only state is the install's files, which the scenarios do not change.
confirmed: stateless route-precedence contract; only the request's method and token vary.
confirmed: the record is stateful false; the two state-dependent effects (isolation, rename freshness) are covered as the edge case instead.
confirmed: Server.js:227-236 has only SIGINT (a second signal exits the process early, which is not an override mode); there is no force/hard shutdown or restart variant to exercise.
confirmed: Logger.js:83-87 delivers by subscription level only; SocketAuthority.js:201-210 has no force/override subscription.
confirmed: BackupManager.js:200-273 applies or rejects an archive; no force/hard parameter exists on the apply route.
confirmed: the event follows a successful BackupManager apply (BackupManager.js:266); there is no force/override emission.
confirmed: BackupManager apply has no force/override variant; an archive is applied or rejected.

open_findings: route-r014: spa-client-routes-serve-entry claims and the invariant requires 'every listed client route', but only /, /library/:id, /library/:id/search, /library/:id/bookshelf[/:id], /library/:id/series, /item/:id, /author/:id, /config/users/:id, /collection/:id and /playlist/:id are exercised; /audiobook/:id/{chapters,edit,manage}, /library/:lib/{authors,narrators,stats}, /library/:lib/podcast/{search,latest,download-queue}, /config/users/:id/sessions, /config/item-metadata-utils/:id and /share/:slug (11 of the 21 Server.js:414-436 routes) are not requested, so a server that omits them still passes.

route-r014: spa-missing-asset-404-no-listing only checks that /favicon.ico's Content-Type is not exactly 'text/html; charset=UTF-8'; upstream sends image/x-icon and the entry document text/html; charset=UTF-8 (verified on the pinned server), so serving the SPA entry (or any 200 bytes) with 'text/html; charset=utf-8' still passes. Assert the icon MIME (image/x-icon) or the fixture file's bytes, otherwise the 'existing asset is served with its own type' element is unproven.

route-r016: libraries-list-and-conditional claims 'serves a random sort without the cache' but asserts only 200 and two entries, which a cache hit returns identically; the element is unobservable and is not in INV-ROUTE-R016-CACHE. Drop the clause or make the bypass observable.

route-r016: the invariant and libraries-user-isolation-and-write-freshness cite server/controllers/LibraryController.js:74-90, which is create() validation; findAll (the accessible-library filter the scenario proves) is LibraryController.js:188-205. Fix the record and scenario source.

protocol-cors-basepath: public-image-exception-boundary claims the ebook answers 401 'even with the mobile CORS grant pre-added' (INV-PROTOCOL-CORS-BASEPATH-PUBLIC-001), but both ebook requests carry no Origin header, so the grant is never present; send Origin: capacitor://localhost (pinned server still answers 401) to prove the grant does not open the ebook route.

runtime-lifecycle: INV-RUNTIME-LIFECYCLE-RESTART-001 says 'a repeated shutdown call keep serving', which contradicts Server.js:227-236 (a second SIGINT exits immediately); repeated-restart-cycles-keep-serving's second Env.Stop is a local no-op (harness/server.go:277-281 returns when no process) and never signals the server. Remove the repeated-shutdown clause or observe a real repeated signal.

runtime-lifecycle: restart-closes-open-sockets-and-welcomes-new claims 'a restart closes an authenticated socket connection', but Env.Stop closes e.sockets client-side before SIGINT (harness/server.go:284-289), so the old socket's server-side closure is never observed; only the new socket's auth+log delivery is asserted. Narrow the claim or assert the old socket's disconnect before the harness closes it.

runtime-lifecycle: shutdown-refuses-requests-not-half-graph (and failed-boot-exits-without-partial-install) use getUnavailable, which returns nil only for status 200 and os.ErrInvalid for any other HTTP answer (scenarios/server/lifecycle.go:16-27); a half-shutdown server that still listens and answers 404/500 therefore passes as 'refusing connections'. Require a transport error (no HTTP response).

runtime-lifecycle: failed-boot-exits-without-partial-install claims the install's config and metadata directories are untouched, but only dirNames(t, broken.Config) is asserted; the metadata directory named in the Claim is never inspected.
